NOw ſtand ye forth my merry men all and hark what I ſhall ſay, Of an aduenture I ſhall you tell the which befell this other day. As I went by the high way with a ſtout Frier I met. And a quarter ſtaffe in his hand, lightly to me he leapt And ſtill he bad me ſtand. there were ſtripes two or three, But I cannot tell who had the worſe but well I wot the whorſon Leapt within me and fro me tooke my purſſe. Is there any of my merry men all that to the Frier will goe, And bring him to me foorth withall whether he will or no. Yeeld thee Frier in thy long cote my throte, I trowe Frier thou beginneſt to dote who made thee ſo malapert and ſo bold, To come into this Forreſt heere, among my fallow deere. Liſten my merry men all and harken what I ſhall ſay, Of an aduenture I ſhall you tell that befell this other day: With a proud potter I met and a roſe garland on his head, the flowers of it ſhone meruailous freſh this ſeuen yeere & more he hath vſed this way Yet was he neuer ſo curteous a potter as one peny paſſage to pay. Is there any of my merry men all that dare be ſo bolde, to make the Potter pay paſſage either ſtluer or golde.
Yes Maiſter I make God auow to that Frier will I goe, And bring him to you whither he will or no,
Deus hic, Deus hic, God be heere is not this a holy word of a Frier, God ſaue all this company, But am not I a iolly Frier For I can ſhoote both farre and neere. and handly the ſword and buckler and this quarter ſtaffe alſo If I meet with a gentle man or yeman, I am not afraid to looke him vpon nor boldly with him to carp • , If he ſpeake any words to me, He ſhall haue ſtripes two or three that ſhall make his body ſmart. But maiſters to ſhew you the matter wherefore and why I am come hither in faith I will not ſpare, I am come to ſeeke a good yeoman in Bernisdale men ſay is his habitation His name is Robin hood And if he be better man then I his ſeruant will I be and ſerue him truly But if that I be a better man then he by my truth my knaue ſhall he be and lead theſe dogges all three.
speeches.Frier tuck: I beſhrew thy hart Knaue thou hurteſt
Goe louſe thee ragged knaue if thou make many words I wil giue thee on y e eare though I be but a poore Frier to ſeeke Robin hood I am come heere and to him my hart to break. thou louſie Frier what wouldſt thou with him he neuer loued Frier nor none of Friers kin.
speeches.Frier: Auaunt ragged knaue or ye ſhall haue on the skin. Auaunt thou ragged knaue this is but a mock if y u make many words y u ſhalt haue a knock, To ſay thee nay I will not to let thee of thine oth it were great pitty & ſin but vpon a Friers back and haue euen in. now am I frier within & thou Robin without, to lay thee heere I haue no great doubt: Now art thou Robin without & I frier within Lye there knaue. chooſe either ſinke or ſwim. Marry ſet a knaue ouer the ſhoon, Why wilt thou fight a pluck Then haue a ſtroke for Frier tuck. Say on ragged knaue me ſeemeth ye begin to ſweat. Blowe on ragged knaue without any doubt, vntill both thine eyes ſtart out: Heere is a ſorte of ragged knaues come in Clothed all in kendall greene and to thee they take their way now. I gaue thee leaue to blow at thy will, now giue me leaue to whiſtle my ſill. Now cut and Bauſe, Bring foorth the clubbes and ſtaues And downe with thoſe ragged knaues. Heere is a huckle duckle an inch aboue the buckle She is a trul of truſt to ſerue a frier at his luſt A pricker, a prauncer, a tearer of ſheetes, a wagger of buttocks when other men ſleeps, Goe home ye knaues and lay crabs in the fier for my lady & I will dance in the mire for very pure ioy.
speeches.Robin hood: Of all the men in a morning thou art y e worſt to meet with thee I haue no luſt, For he y t meeteth a frier or a fox in the morning to ſpeede ill that day he ſtandeth in ieopardie therefore I had rather meet with the deuill Frier I tell thee as I think, then meete with a frier or a fox in a morning or I drinke. Hark frier what I ſay heere, ouer this water thou ſhalt me beare the bridge is borne away. Nay haue ouer. Why thou louſie frier what haſt thou doon Therefor thou ſhalt abye And God ſend me good luck, Holde thy hand Frier and heare me ſpeak In this Forreſt I haue a hound I will not giue him for an hundreth pound: Giue me leaue my horne to blowe, that my hound may know. Peraduenture they doe ſo Whiſtle Frier euill might thou fare, vntill both thine eyes ſtare. How ſaiſt thou Frier wilt thou be my man to doo me the beſt ſeruice thou can, Thou ſhalt haue both gold and fee, And alſo heer is a lady free I will giue hir vn to thee And her chaplain I thee make to ſerue her for my ſake. I will lay with thee little Iohn xx. pound ſo red if I with the potter meet I will make him pay paſſage mauger his hed. Little Iohn where art thou,
speeches.Little Iohn: Not I maiſter for twenty pound ready tolde For there is not amongſt vs all one that dare meddle with that potter man for man I felt his hands not long agon but I had leuer be heere by thee, therefore I know what he is Meete him when ye will or meete him when you ſhall, He is as proper a man as euer you medled withall I conſent thereto ſo I eat bread, If he pay paſſage mauger his head twenty pound ſhall ye haue for your meed. Here maiſter I make auow I toulde you maiſter ſo God me ſaue, that you ſhould finde the potter a knaue: Holde your buckler faſt in your hand, and I will ſtiffely by you ſtand, Ready for to fight, Be the knaue neuer ſo ſtout I ſhall rap him on the ſnout, and put him to flight.
Out alas that euer I ſaw this day. For I am cleane out of my way: From Nottingham towne, If I me hie not the faſter Or I come there the market will be doon.
speeches.Robin: Let me ſee are thy pots whole and ſound. I will them break-for the cuckold thy maſters And if they will break the ground thou ſhalt haue three pence for a pound. Hark potter what I ſhall ſay. this 7. yeer and more thou haſt vſed this way Yet were thou neuer ſo curteous to me as one peny paſſage to pay. For I am Robin hood cheefe gouernour vnder the greene-wood tree. Paſſage ſhalt thou pay heere vnder the green woodtree or els thou ſhalt leaue a wed with me:
speeches.Iack: Yea maiſter but they will not breake y e ground ſake Out alas what haue you doon if my maiſter come he will breake your crowne I met with Robin hood a good yeman He hath broken my pottes and cald you Cuckold by your name.
speeches.the Potter: Why thou whorſon art thou heere yet thou ſhouldeſt haue been at market.
speeches.Potter: Thou maiſt be a gentleman ſo God me ſaue, but thou ſeemeſt a naughty knaue: Thou calleſt me a cuckold by my name. And I ſwere by God and ſaint Iohn. Wife had I neuer none this cannot I deny But if thou be a good fellow I will ſell my horſe harnes, pots & paniers too thou ſhalt haue the one halfe and I the other if thou be not ſo content thou ſhalt haue ſtripes if thou were my brother. Why ſhould I pay paſſage to thee, This ſeuen yere I vſed this way vp and down yet payed I paſſage to no man, Nor now I will not begin do the worſt y u can. Yf thou be a good fellow as men doo thee call, laye away thy bowe And take thy ſword and buckler in thy hand and ſee what ſhall befall.
